If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in the mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in the early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% in the late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across 3+ days, apply a flat correction of ±0.5% to forecast in late horizon to avoid overfitting to recent noise.  
In cases where model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in early horizon, reduce forecast by 2–4% in mid-horizon to dampen early overestimation.  
If true outcome shows a sharp upward trend (≥2% per day) in late horizon, reduce forecast by 1–3% in late horizon if sentiment is weak (≤0.33) to prevent overcorrection.
